questions.stem: The average of \(5\) consecutive numbers is \(12\). What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.keySolution:
Let the consecutive numbers be \(n-2, n-1, n, n+1, n+2\)
Sum = \(5n = 12 \times 5 = 60\)
Therefore, \(n = 12\)
The numbers are \(10, 11, 12, 13, 14\)
Largest number = \(14\)

questions.stem: The average of \(7\) consecutive even numbers is \(16\). What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.keySolution:
For \(7\) consecutive even numbers, the middle (4th) number equals the average
Middle number = \(16\)
The numbers are: \(10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22\)
Smallest number = \(10\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(4\) consecutive odd numbers is \(18\), what is the sum of the first and last numbers?
questions.keySolution:
Let the numbers be \(n, n+2, n+4, n+6\)
Average = \(\frac{4n+12}{4} = 18\)
\(n+3 = 18\), so \(n = 15\)
Numbers are \(15, 17, 19, 21\)
Sum of first and last = \(15 + 21 = 36\)

questions.stem: The average of \(6\) consecutive numbers is \(22.5\). What is the difference between the largest and smallest numbers?
questions.keySolution:
For \(6\) consecutive numbers, average = \(\frac{(first + last)}{2} = 22.5\)
First + last = \(45\)
Let first number = \(n\), then last = \(n+5\)
\(n + (n+5) = 45\), so \(n = 20\)
Difference = \((n+5) - n = 5\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(9\) consecutive numbers is \(45\), what is the median of these numbers?
questions.keySolution:
For odd number of consecutive terms, median = average
Median = \(45\)

questions.stem: The average of \(3\) consecutive even numbers is \(24\). If a fourth consecutive even number is added, what will be the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Original numbers: \(22, 24, 26\) (average = \(24\))
Fourth number = \(28\)
New sum = \(22 + 24 + 26 + 28 = 100\)
New average = \(\frac{100}{4} = 25\)

questions.stem: The sum of \(5\) consecutive numbers is \(85\). What is the middle number?
questions.keySolution:
Average = \(\frac{85}{5} = 17\)
For odd number of consecutive terms, middle term = average = \(17\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(8\) consecutive even numbers is \(19\), what is the largest number?
questions.keySolution:
For \(8\) consecutive even numbers, average = \(\frac{4th + 5th}{2} = 19\)
4th + 5th = \(38\)
Let 4th term = \(n\), then 5th = \(n+2\)
\(2n + 2 = 38\), so \(n = 18\)
Numbers: \(12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26\)
Largest = \(26\)

questions.stem: The average of \(4\) consecutive numbers is \(15.5\). If the smallest number is removed, what will be the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Original sum = \(15.5 \times 4 = 62\)
Numbers are \(14, 15, 16, 17\) (average between 2nd and 3rd = \(15.5\))
After removing \(14\): sum = \(15 + 16 + 17 = 48\)
New average = \(\frac{48}{3} = 16\)

questions.stem: If the average of first \(n\) consecutive natural numbers is \(15\), what is the value of \(n\)?
questions.keySolution:
Average of first \(n\) natural numbers = \(\frac{n+1}{2} = 15\)
\(n + 1 = 30\)
\(n = 29\)

questions.stem: The average of \(7\) consecutive odd numbers is \(33\). What is the sum of the largest and smallest numbers?
questions.keySolution:
Middle (4th) number = \(33\)
Numbers: \(27, 29, 31, 33, 35, 37, 39\)
Sum of largest and smallest = \(39 + 27 = 66\)

questions.stem: If \(5\) consecutive even numbers have an average of \(28\), what is their product's units digit?
questions.keySolution:
Numbers: \(24, 26, 28, 30, 32\)
Product = \(24 \times 26 \times 28 \times 30 \times 32\)
Since \(30\) is a multiple of \(10\), the product ends in \(0\)

questions.stem: The average of \(6\) consecutive numbers is \(17.5\). If each number is increased by \(3\), what will be the new average?
questions.keySolution:
When each number is increased by the same amount, average increases by that amount
New average = \(17.5 + 3 = 20.5\)

questions.stem: If the sum of \(4\) consecutive odd numbers is \(80\), what is the largest number?
The average of \(10\) consecutive numbers is \(25.5\). What is the \(8\)th number in the sequence?

questions.keySolution:

questions.stem: The sum of \(7\) consecutive even numbers is \(182\). What is the middle number?
questions.keySolution:
Average = \(\frac{182}{7} = 26\)
For odd number of consecutive terms, middle term = average = \(26\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(5\) consecutive numbers is \(x\), what is the sum of the \(2\)nd and \(4\)th numbers in terms of \(x\)?
questions.keySolution:
Let numbers be \(n-2, n-1, n, n+1, n+2\) where \(n = x\)
2nd number = \(x-1\)
4th number = \(x+1\)
Sum = \((x-1) + (x+1) = 2x\)

questions.stem: The average of \(4\) consecutive even numbers is \(27\). By adding which number does the average become \(28\)?
If \(6\) consecutive odd numbers have a sum of \(126\), what is the difference between the largest and the average?
questions.keySolution:
Average = \(\frac{126}{6} = 21\)
For \(6\) consecutive odd numbers: \(15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25\)
Largest = \(25\)
Difference = \(25 - 21 = 4\)

questions.stem: The product of \(3\) consecutive numbers is \(504\). What is their average?
questions.keySolution:
Let numbers be \(n-1, n, n+1\)
Product = \(n(n-1)(n+1) = n(n^2-1) = 504\)
Trying \(n = 8\): \(8 \times 63 = 504\) ✓
Numbers: \(7, 8, 9\)
Average = \(8\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(11\) consecutive even numbers is \(22\), what is the \(6\)th number?
questions.keySolution: For \(11\) consecutive numbers, the 6th (middle) number = average = \(22\)

questions.stem: The sum of first and last of \(9\) consecutive numbers is \(56\). What is their average?
questions.keySolution:
For consecutive numbers: first + last = \(2 \times\) average
Average = \(\frac{56}{2} = 28\)

questions.stem: If \(8\) consecutive numbers have an average of \(12.5\), what is the sum of the \(3\)rd and \(6\)th numbers?
The average of \(5\) consecutive multiples of \(3\) is \(21\). What is the largest number?
questions.keySolution:
Middle number = \(21\)
Numbers: \(15, 18, 21, 24, 27\)
Largest = \(27\)

questions.stem: If the sum of \(6\) consecutive even numbers is \(150\), what is the smallest number?
questions.keySolution:
Average = \(\frac{150}{6} = 25\)
For \(6\) consecutive even numbers, average = \(\frac{3rd + 4th}{2} = 25\)
3rd + 4th = \(50\)
Let 3rd = \(n\), then 4th = \(n+2\)
\(2n + 2 = 50\), so \(n = 24\)
Smallest = \(24 - 4 = 20\)

questions.stem: The average of \(7\) consecutive numbers starting from \(n\) is \(15\). What is the value of \(n\)?
If \(4\) consecutive odd numbers have an average of \(16\), what is the product of the middle two numbers?
questions.keySolution:
For \(4\) consecutive odd numbers, average = \(\frac{2nd + 3rd}{2} = 16\)
2nd + 3rd = \(32\)
Let 2nd = \(n\), then 3rd = \(n+2\)
\(2n + 2 = 32\), so \(n = 15\)
Middle numbers: \(15, 17\)
Product = \(15 \times 17 = 255\)

questions.stem: The average of \(12\) consecutive numbers is \(18.5\). What is the sum of the first \(6\) numbers?
If the average of \(n\) consecutive even numbers starting from \(2\) is \(51\), what is \(n\)?
The sum of \(5\) consecutive odd numbers is \(95\). If the middle number is removed, what is the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Average = \(\frac{95}{5} = 19\) (middle number)
Numbers: \(15, 17, 19, 21, 23\)
After removing \(19\): sum = \(15 + 17 + 21 + 23 = 76\)
New average = \(\frac{76}{4} = 19\)

questions.stem: If \(3\) consecutive multiples of \(5\) have an average of \(25\), what is their sum?
questions.keySolution: Sum = Average × Count = \(25 \times 3 = 75\)

questions.stem: The average of \(6\) consecutive numbers is \(23.5\). If the largest number is replaced by \(35\), what is the new average?

questions.keySolution:

For \(8\) consecutive even numbers, average = \(\frac{4th + 5th}{2} = 25\)
4th + 5th = \(50\)
Let 4th = \(n\), then 5th = \(n+2\)
\(2n + 2 = 50\), so \(n = 24\)

questions.stem: The average of \(9\) consecutive odd numbers is \(41\). What is the sum of the first three numbers?

questions.stem: The average of \(7\) consecutive even numbers is \(30\). If each number is doubled, what will be the new average?
questions.keySolution:
When each number is doubled, the average is also doubled
New average = \(30 \times 2 = 60\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(4\) consecutive multiples of \(7\) is \(35\), what is the smallest number?
questions.keySolution:
Let numbers be \(7a, 7(a+1), 7(a+2), 7(a+3)\)
Sum = \(7(4a+6) = 35 \times 4 = 140\)
\(4a + 6 = 20\), so \(a = 3.5\)
Numbers are \(24.5, 31.5, 38.5, 45.5\) - but these aren't multiples!
Let me recalculate: \(28, 35, 42, 49\) (average = \(38.5\))
Actually: \(21, 28, 35, 42\) (average = \(31.5\))
For average \(35\): \(28, 35, 42, 49\) doesn't work
Correct: \(28, 35, 42, 49\) average = \(38.5\)
But given average is \(35\), so numbers are \(21, 28, 35, 42\)
Smallest = \(21\)

questions.stem: The sum of \(10\) consecutive numbers is \(245\). What is the average of the first \(5\) numbers?

questions.stem: The average of \(8\) consecutive numbers is \(15.5\). If the first and last numbers are removed, what is the new average?
If the product of \(2\) consecutive even numbers is \(168\), what is their average?
questions.keySolution:
Let numbers be \(n\) and \(n+2\)
\(n(n+2) = 168\)
\(n^2 + 2n - 168 = 0\)
Solving: \(n = 12\) or \(n = -14\)
Taking positive: numbers are \(12, 14\)
Average = \(\frac{12+14}{2} = 13\)

questions.stem: The average of \(5\) consecutive numbers is \(n\). What is the sum of the largest and second smallest numbers in terms of \(n\)?
questions.keySolution:
Numbers: \(n-2, n-1, n, n+1, n+2\)
Largest = \(n+2\)
Second smallest = \(n-1\)
Sum = \((n+2) + (n-1) = 2n + 1\)

questions.stem: If \(7\) consecutive multiples of \(4\) have a sum of \(168\), what is the middle number?
questions.keySolution:
Average = \(\frac{168}{7} = 24\)
For odd number of consecutive terms, middle term = average = \(24\)

questions.stem: The average of \(4\) consecutive even numbers is \(23\). What is the sum of the \(1\)st and \(3\)rd numbers?
questions.keySolution:
For \(4\) consecutive even numbers, average = \(\frac{2nd + 3rd}{2} = 23\)
2nd + 3rd = \(46\)
Let 2nd = \(n\), then 3rd = \(n+2\)
\(2n + 2 = 46\), so \(n = 22\)
Numbers: \(20, 22, 24, 26\)
1st + 3rd = \(20 + 24 = 44\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(9\) consecutive numbers starting from \(a\) is \(50\), what is the value of \(a\)?
The sum of \(3\) consecutive even numbers is \(54\). If each number is increased by \(5\), what will be the new sum?
questions.keySolution:
Original sum = \(54\)
Increase = \(5 \times 3 = 15\)
New sum = \(54 + 15 = 69\)

questions.stem: If \(6\) consecutive numbers have an average of \(15.5\), what is the product of the \(2\)nd and \(5\)th numbers?
questions.keySolution:
Numbers: \(13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18\)
2nd number = \(14\)
5th number = \(17\)
Product = \(14 \times 17 = 238\)

questions.stem: The average of \(10\) consecutive odd numbers is \(26\). What is the \(7\)th number in the sequence?
questions.keySolution:
For \(10\) consecutive odd numbers, average = \(\frac{5th + 6th}{2} = 26\)
5th + 6th = \(52\)
Let 5th = \(n\), then 6th = \(n+2\)
\(2n + 2 = 52\), so \(n = 25\)
7th number = \(25 + 4 = 29\)
